#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh — the whole-stage time limit (ADR-063, amended
# 2026-10-15). Read from the loaded template (_TPL_SOURCE_FILE, exported by
# load_template), so every dispatch arm — the map arm's generated script
# included — sees the same value.
#
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_TIME_LIMIT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_TIME_LIMIT_LOADED=1

# Per-stage `timeout_s:` — how long the engine lets the WHOLE stage run before
# it stops it (every model call, check and retry inside it). Not router.timeout_s,
# which bounds one model call. 900 seconds (15 minutes) when unset. Read lazily
# from the template source, like template_stage_retry.
template_stage_time_limit() {
    local _tstl; template_stage_time_limit_v _tstl "$1"; printf '%s' "$_tstl"
}
# template_stage_time_limit_v <var> <stage> — the same into <var>. One read of
# the template gives every stage's limit (template_stage_time_limits_load), and
# load_template makes that read in the runner's shell, so every dispatch
# inherits it (ADR-065 §5): asked per stage, the read was redone in each
# dispatch's subshell.
declare -gA _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO=()   # "<template>\034<stage>" → its timeout_s text; "<template>\034" → read
template_stage_time_limit_v() {
    local -n _tstv="$1"
    template_stage_time_limits_load
    _tstv="${_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}"$'\034'"$2"]:-}"
    [[ "$_tstv" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || _tstv=900
}

# template_stage_time_limits_load — every stage's `timeout_s:` from the template,
# in one pass, into _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO; once per template (…_reload reads again).
# A stage's limit is its block's own `timeout_s:` one level in: the block opens
# at `<stage>:` in column 0, or two deep under `stage_definitions:`, and closes
# at the next line no deeper than its header; the first such line wins, and a
# block can open again further down. Every stage is followed at once, rule for
# rule as the per-stage reader this replaces (tests/unit/shell-work-cost-test.sh
# W5 holds the two equal).
template_stage_time_limits_load() {
    local f="${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}"
    [[ -n "$f" ]] || return 0
    [[ -n "${_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034']+x}" ]] && return 0
    _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034']=1
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
    local line lead li in_defs=0 s s1 s4 s4_was v
    local -A open=() ind=() found=()
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^stage_definitions:[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then in_defs=1; continue; fi
        lead="${line%%[! ]*}"; li=${#lead}
        s1=""; [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):[[:space:]]*$ ]] && s1="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        (( in_defs )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_] ]] && in_defs=0
        s4=""; (( in_defs )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^\ \ ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):[[:space:]]*$ ]] && s4="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        s4_was="${s4:+${open[$s4]:-}}"
        for s in "${!open[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ [^[:space:]] ]] && (( li <= ind[$s] )); then unset 'open[$s]'; continue; fi
            if (( li == ind[$s] + 2 )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:[[:space:]]* ]]; then
                v="${line:${#BASH_REMATCH[0]}}"
                if [[ "$v" == *#* ]]; then v="${v%%#*}"; v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"; fi
                _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034'"$s"]="${v//[[:space:]]/}"
                found[$s]=1; unset 'open[$s]'
            fi
        done
        if [[ -n "$s1" && -z "${found[$s1]:-}" ]]; then open[$s1]=1; ind[$s1]=0; fi
        if [[ -n "$s4" && -z "${found[$s4]:-}" && -z "$s4_was" ]]; then open[$s4]=1; ind[$s4]=2; fi
    done 2>/dev/null < "$f"
}

# template_stage_time_limits_reload — forget the template's limits and read it
# again: load_template's call, as the file may have changed since it was read.
template_stage_time_limits_reload() {
    local f="${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" k
    [[ -n "$f" ]] || return 0
    for k in "${!_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO[@]}"; do
        [[ "$k" == "$f"$'\034'* ]] && unset "_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO[$k]"
    done
    template_stage_time_limits_load
}

11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#

94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"

128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"

132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0

138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}

146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.

153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"

157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"

162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"

# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
    # as an option.
    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
    done
    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
_zbuild_pg_grace() {
    local _g="${1:-1}"
    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
}

# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
#
# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
#
# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
}

# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
#
# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
#
# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
#
# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
#
# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
zbuild_pg_register() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
    local _start
    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
zbuild_pg_kill() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
zbuild_pid_kill() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0 timed_out_flag=false
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                timed_out_flag=true
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif $timed_out_flag; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"
        return 1
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}
